items.abstract: <jats:p>Cyclopia, is an extremely rare congenital condition resulting from severe disruption of early brain and facial development and is typically lethal before or shortly after birth. We examined two infants buried together in a Middle Nasca-period cemetery in Jauranga, southern Peru. One infant, JA13A, exhibited a single median orbit and other skeletal features diagnostic of cyclopia, whereas JA13B showed no comparable congenital variations. Ancient DNA revealed an extra copy of chromosome 13 in JA13A, identifying trisomy 13 as the likely cause. The two maternally unrelated individuals were interred together in a ceramic vessel, a mortuary treatment well documented for Nasca children. By integrating skeletal, genomic, and archaeological evidence, this case provides a view of a severe congenital condition and its mortuary treatment in a past society.</jats:p>
items.summary: 《纳斯卡时期围产期墓葬揭示秘鲁南部与13三体相关的独眼畸形》：研究通过古DNA发现，秘鲁南部Jauranga中纳斯卡时期墓地合葬的两名婴儿中，JA13A具有单一眼眶等独眼畸形骨骼特征，并检出13号染色体多一份，提示13三体为可能病因；两名母系无关婴儿同置陶器合葬，结合骨骼、基因组与考古证据，呈现了古代社会对严重先天性疾病及其丧葬处理的认识，值得关注。
items.title: A Nasca-period perinatal burial reveals cyclopia associated with trisomy 13 in southern Peru

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Reconstructing dietary practices in prehistoric hunter‐gatherer populations requires disentangling complex ecological, cultural, and chronological variables. In the Cis‐Baikal region of Siberia, subsistence systems relied on combinations of freshwater and terrestrial resources, including fish, Baikal seals, and terrestrial game. This study integrates zinc isotope ratios (δ
                      <jats:sup>66</jats:sup>
                      Zn) from mineralized tissues with compound‐specific nitrogen isotope analysis of amino acids (CSIA‐AA) to evaluate the potential of δ
                      <jats:sup>66</jats:sup>
                      Zn to document trophic structure and dietary resource use in prehistoric human populations, with faunal data providing the ecological context across three microregions: Angara, Southwest Baikal, and the Little Sea.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Materials and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      We analyzed δ
                      <jats:sup>66</jats:sup>
                      Zn values measured in dental enamel, dentin, and bone, together with CSIA‐AA nitrogen isotope data, from humans and associated fauna from three Cis‐Baikal microregions. Fish were classified into dietary clusters based on ecological feeding strategies to assess relationships between δ
                      <jats:sup>66</jats:sup>
                      Zn, diet, and trophic position.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Among human populations, zinc isotope ratios provide a sensitive proxy for identifying seal consumption within mixed subsistence systems. Phenylalanine nitrogen isotope values (δ
                      <jats:sup>15</jats:sup>
                      N
                      <jats:sub>Phe</jats:sub>
                      ) discriminate between terrestrial and aquatic protein baselines. In freshwater fishes, δ
                      <jats:sup>66</jats:sup>
                      Zn values vary primarily according to dietary ecology rather than trophic level, indicating that dietary Zn isotope composition exerts a stronger control on tissue δ
                      <jats:sup>66</jats:sup>
                      Zn than trophic position.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The combined use of δ
                      <jats:sup>66</jats:sup>
                      Zn and CSIA‐AA refines dietary interpretations in complex terrestrial–freshwater ecosystems by disentangling baselines, trophic structure, and specific resource use. These findings demonstrate the utility of combining δ
                      <jats:sup>66</jats:sup>
                      Zn and CSIA‐AA to improve reconstructions of subsistence strategies in the studied prehistoric populations.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
items.summary: 《利用锌与氨基酸氮同位素对贝加尔湖西岸史前饮食与营养结构的多元同位素重建》：该研究结合牙齿与骨骼的锌同位素比值及氨基酸氮同位素分析，评估锌同位素在识别海豹消费、区分陆生与水生蛋白基线方面的作用，并发现淡水鱼锌同位素主要随饮食生态而非营养级变化，值得关注史前生计与同位素方法的研究者阅读。
items.title: Multi‐Isotopic Reconstruction of Prehistoric Diet and Trophic Organization in Cis‐Baikal Using Zinc and Amino Acid Nitrogen Isotopes

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Collective memory shapes how societies respond to extreme climate events, yet long-term evidence on how the collective memory of such events becomes perceptually biased over time is lacking. Here, we utilise four centuries (1470–1900) of climatic archives from northern China, along with tree–ring–based hydroclimate reconstructions, which are validated against instrumental observations of Wet/Dry Index (1901–2000) to fill the gap. We find that historical records reveal systematic, non-random mismatches, where severity assessments are often biased toward recent experience rather than absolute climatic anomalies. Correlations between historical and natural records increase when the natural series is re-standardised using 20–40-year sliding windows, reflecting a generational offset. A heuristic agent-based model reproduces this pattern, suggesting that generational amnesia is sufficient to explain the offsets in perception of environmental change. We argue that historical archives carry a generational imprint of perceptual bias, in which the severity of climate extremes is judged against recent lived experience rather than long-term climate variability. This has implications for bias-aware corrections for risk assessment, adaptation, and paleoclimate reconstruction.</jats:p>
items.summary: 《极端气候事件的档案与古环境记录揭示集体记忆中的代际遗忘》：研究利用中国北方1470至1900年的气候档案与树轮水文气候重建，发现历史记录对气候极端事件严重程度的评估常偏向近期经验而非绝对气候异常，并呈现20至40年的代际偏移，启发式主体模型表明代际遗忘足以解释这一感知偏差，值得关注其对风险评估、适应与古气候重建的启示。
items.title: Archival and palaeoenvironmental documentation of extreme climate events reveals generational amnesia in collective memory

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The hypothesis that temperate tree taxa survived the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM; 26.5–19 ka cal BP) in cryptic northern refugia has significant implications for European biogeography and postglacial vegetation history. Recently, sedimentary ancient DNA recovered from offshore sediment cores in the Southern River System of the North Sea Basin has been interpreted as evidence for the local persistence of temperate woodland taxa during the LGM. This review critically evaluates that hypothesis by synthesising the currently available palaeobotanical and sedimentary ancient DNA evidence from the North Sea Basin and adjacent terrestrial regions. Independent palaeoclimate reconstructions consistently indicate cold, dry conditions, continuous permafrost and temperatures well below the ecological requirements of temperate woodland trees. These reconstructions are broadly congruent with pollen, plant macrofossil, vertebrate and coleopteran records, which collectively indicate the persistence of low‐productivity arctic to subarctic steppe–tundra vegetation throughout the region during the LGM. This strong convergence among independent palaeoenvironmental datasets contrasts with limited support for the local persistence of temperate woodland communities throughout the LGM in the North Sea Basin.</jats:p>
items.summary: 《温带树木在末次盛冰期是否存活于北海盆地？对现有证据的批判性评述》：该文综合北海盆地及邻近陆域的古植物学与沉积物古DNA证据，检验温带树种在末次盛冰期于当地隐秘避难所存活的假说，指出独立古气候重建与多类化石记录一致显示当时为寒冷干燥的永久冻土环境、植被为低生产力极地至亚极地草原苔原，对该假说支持有限，适合关注欧洲生物地理与冰期植被史的读者阅读。
items.title: Did temperate trees survive the Last Glacial Maximum in the North Sea Basin? A critical review of current evidence

items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">The Paleocene-Eocene transition is marked by dramatic global climatic change correlated with pronounced mammalian faunal change. A new late Paleocene mammal fauna from the Butte de Therdonne in the Paris Basin is described and compared with fossil assemblages of similar age elsewhere in Europe and North America. The Therdonne fauna is currently documented by c. 45 identifiable fossil specimens representing nine mammalian species. The stratigraphic position of this fossil assemblage in the early Paleogene Therdonne sequence indicates a late Thanetian age, and the taxonomic assemblage is consistent with the MP6b reference biochronological level defined on the basis of a mammalian fauna found in the Rivecourt sand Member in the Oise Valley, about 40 km east of Therdonne. The relative diversity of rodents and condylarthrans including the North American apheliscid Aletodon Gingerich, 1977, are the most striking characteristics of this fauna. Several lines of evidence, including biostratigraphy, sequence stratigraphic interpretation of the Therdonne section, and correlations with boreholes of the Paris Basin lead us to correlate the Therdonne and Rivecourt faunas. Therdonne therefore pertains to the MP6b biozone which corresponds roughly to the 1 Ma interval preceding the onset of the carbon isotope excursion (CIE) that marks the Paleocene-Eocene boundary.</jats:p>
items.summary: 《法国瓦兹省泰尔东地区新发现的晚坦尼特期哺乳动物群：西欧存在克拉克福克期等效生物带的 new 证据》：该研究描述了巴黎盆地泰尔东丘一处晚古新世哺乳动物群，约45件可鉴定标本隶属9个哺乳动物种，其地层位置指示晚坦尼特期，动物群特征与MP6b参考生物年代带一致，并据此将泰尔东与里沃库尔动物群对比，认为泰尔东归属MP6b生物带，大致对应古新世-始新世边界碳同位素…
items.title: A new late Thanetian mammal fauna from Therdonne (Oise, France): new evidence for a Clarkforkian-equivalent biozone in Western Europe

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Understanding how reproductive isolation is maintained between closely related taxa is a central question in evolutionary biology. Here, we investigate the mechanisms underlying divergence and isolation between two sister butterflies,
                    <jats:italic>Erebia palarica</jats:italic>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>Erebia meolans</jats:italic>
                    , which occur in sympatry in the Cantabrian Mountains (N Spain) and in allopatry elsewhere. Using an integrative approach, we combine genetic, genome synteny and cytogenetic analyses,
                    <jats:italic>Wolbachia</jats:italic>
                    screening, and geometric morphometrics to assess their evolutionary history and elucidate potential reproductive barriers between these species. The phylogeographic pattern suggests that both species diverged in allopatry, coming into secondary contact along the Cantabrian Mountains after the last glacial maximum. Both mitochondrial and nuclear markers recover reciprocal monophyly, indicating the absence of recent hybridisation. The identical chromosome numbers in both species (2
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                     = 28), the absence of major chromosomal rearrangements or straightforward genitalia differentiation, and the presence of the same
                    <jats:italic>Wolbachia</jats:italic>
                    strain in all infected individuals suggest that neither chromosomal rearrangements nor
                    <jats:italic>Wolbachia</jats:italic>
                    ‐induced incompatibilities contribute to their reproductive isolation in sympatry. In contrast, morphometric analyses show a significant divergence in wing size consistent with asymmetric character displacement: sympatric populations of
                    <jats:italic>E. palarica</jats:italic>
                    exhibit larger wings relative to both allopatric conspecifics and sympatric
                    <jats:italic>E. meolans</jats:italic>
                    , whereas
                    <jats:italic>E. meolans</jats:italic>
                    shows little size variation across northern Spain. Our findings point to wing size divergence in
                    <jats:italic>E. palarica</jats:italic>
                    as a response to sympatry with
                    <jats:italic>E. meolans</jats:italic>
                    . Overall, this study provides novel empirical evidence for morphometric character displacement in the family Nymphalidae, highlights the importance of multidisciplinary approaches for understanding species differentiation, and sets a framework for future genomic studies of speciation and reproductive isolation between closely related taxa.
                  </jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) provides motor innervation to all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except the cricothyroid. Detailed knowledge of its terminal branching is essential for thyroid, laryngeal, and voice surgeons. This review synthesizes existing human cadaveric and surgical descriptions of the extralaryngeal and motor branching of the RLN, with attention to functional and clinical implications. Prior to laryngeal entry, the RLN most commonly bifurcates into an anterior (motor) and posterior (sensory) branch, with extralaryngeal branching identified in approximately 60% of nerves across large pooled series; bifurcation accounts for roughly half of all cases and typically occurs 1–2 cm inferior to the cricothyroid articulation. The motor division of the RLN is organized into vertical, genu, and oblique segments. The posterior cricoarytenoid muscle, the sole abductor of the true vocal fold, is innervated first and exhibits at least three distinct branching configurations, with further complexity arising from compartmental innervation patterns. The adductor muscles—arytenoid, lateral cricoarytenoid, and thyroarytenoid—are innervated sequentially, with the branches to the latter two representing the true terminal branches of the RLN. These branches form a complex anastomotic network with the superior laryngeal nerve, including Galen's anastomosis and the arytenoid plexus. Current anatomical knowledge derives predominantly from small cadaveric series; further studies are needed for characterization of these structures with greater resolution and clinical applicability.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The posterior cricoarytenoid muscle (PCA) is the only intrinsic laryngeal muscle that abducts the vocal fold and is therefore a key target for selective reinnervation in bilateral vocal fold paralysis. Because its distal nerve supply is anatomically variable, direct implantation strategies may benefit from precise knowledge of motor endplate topography. We characterized the spatial distribution of motor endplates in bilateral posterior cricoarytenoid muscles obtained from five human body donors (
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                     = 5; four men and one woman; median age 80 years, range 79–98), yielding a total of 10 muscles for descriptive anatomical analysis. One left PCA was affected by documented unilateral vocal fold paralysis and was analyzed separately. Motor endplates were labeled with tetramethylrhodamine‐conjugated α‐bungarotoxin, imaged by whole‐slide fluorescence scanning, and detected using a standardized QuPath workflow. In the nine muscles without known laryngeal pathology, motor endplates were heterogeneously distributed, with higher‐density regions frequently forming an arcuate band. The vertical compartment contained a median of 71.5% of all detected endplates (range 52.8–87.3%) and showed a median areal density of 3.57 endplates/mm
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    , compared with 2.43 endplates/mm
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    in the horizontal compartment. Muscle fibers bearing multiple motor endplates were also observed. The paralyzed PCA showed high motor endplate density across a broader portion of the muscle, with less clearly defined spatial zonation. These findings support the existence of preferential motor endplate zones in the human PCA, while highlighting substantial anatomical variability, particularly in the pathological specimen. This variability may have implications for the positioning of donor nerve implants during selective laryngeal reinnervation.
                  </jats:p>
